reasons.text: Both parts have the same sheet metal type, material, size, unit of measure, make/buy setting and Released lifecycle, so they appear to describe the same physical plate.
The export classifications conflict (9A610.x versus EAR99) across different business units, so merging without review could misclassify a controlled part or over-control an uncontrolled one.
The weights are close but not identical (1.430 versus 1.403), which looks like a possible digit transposition, but it should be confirmed.
If confirmed as the same part, 210-004256 would be the one to keep because it is used in more assemblies and is older, while 210-008577 is unused.

before_merging: Have export compliance confirm the correct classification for the plate (9A610.x vs EAR99) before any merge, since the retained part's classification will apply to all usages.
Confirm with J. Adeyemi and A. Novak that the two plates share identical geometry, features and finish beyond the listed size and material.
Verify the correct weight, since the recorded values differ (1.430 vs 1.403) and should be checked against the plate's dimensions and material.
Confirm whether the Aerospace Systems design carries any aerospace-specific requirements that make it unsuitable as a direct replacement for the Industrial Controls part, or vice versa.
